comments.note: AC UNMET: 'Header renders with Title=Library Folders visible.' MainContentView.axaml has no Header attribute on the NavigationView element, and MainContentView.axaml.cs has no NavView.Header assignment anywhere. With FluentAvalonia NavigationView, the Header property is NOT auto-populated from the selected item — it must be set explicitly. The header area will be blank at runtime. Fix: bind Header in AXAML (e.g., Header="{Binding [ActiveDestinationTitle]}") or assign NavView.Header inside UpdateSelectedItem() / OnActiveDestinationChanged() using the destination's Title. Note: this AC is not present in the WP-011.md spec file — it appears to have been added to the ledger separately. Developer should confirm with PM whether this AC is intentional; if not, PM should remove it from the ledger.

AC UNVERIFIABLE: 'Back button not shown when Library Folders is a primary rail destination at root stack depth.' No IsBackButtonVisible or IsBackEnabled is set anywhere in the codebase. Whether the back button is hidden depends entirely on FluentAvalonia's defaults (IsBackButtonVisible=Auto, IsBackEnabled=false — expected result: back button auto-hidden). Cannot confirm without running the app. Developer should either verify via manual test or add an explicit IsBackButtonVisible="Collapsed" attribute to the NavigationView, or write a headless test. Note: this AC is also not in the WP-011.md spec file.

Spec discrepancy: WP-011.md contains only 5 ACs. The ledger contains 7 ACs. The 2 extra ACs ('Header visible', 'Back button not shown') are not in the spec file but are in the ledger as unmet. The developer addressed only the 5 spec ACs and declared PASS. PM should reconcile the spec and ledger ACs to prevent future confusion.

comments.note: MainContentView.axaml.cs constructor: OnNavViewSelectionChanged is subscribed twice — once via SelectionChanged="OnNavViewSelectionChanged" in AXAML (wired in InitializeComponent()) and once explicitly via NavView.SelectionChanged += OnNavViewSelectionChanged in the constructor body. This causes NavigateTo() to be called twice on every user click. The _updatingSelection guard only protects programmatic updates; it does not guard against double-fire on user gestures. If NavigateTo is idempotent this is benign, but the double subscription is a latent defect. Pre-existing from the original implementation — not introduced by the rework. Recommend removing the duplicate subscription from the constructor.
